text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Victorian Supreme Court yesterday issued an interim injunction restraining the Flight Attendants Association from organising any form of industrial action by its members at Ansett. The decision leaves the door open for other employers to bypass requirements under rederal industrial laws that they spend 72 hours in conciliation proceedings in the Industrial Relations Commission before taking common law action against unions. Page 1.

Federal Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser said yesterday the Small Business Deregulations Task Force report should include some radical suggestions to slash the amount of paperwork required for small businesses and solve the compliance problems within the sector. Page 2.

The Industry Commission annual report claims micro-economic reform has not destroyed jobs over the past decade and suggests reform willd provide employment opportunities for the unemployed over the longer term. The report also says the business cycle was responsible for most change in the labour market. Page 3.

Federal Primary Industries and Energy Minister John Anderson has announced new three-year woodchip export licences in an attempt to avoid the annual controversy over logging in native forests. The decision has been criticised by Greens Senator Bob Brown who claimed it had "set the seal on the destruction of Australian forests." Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Independent MP Pauline Hanson issued a challenge to Parliament yesterday, claiming the previous day's parliamentary debate on a motion deploring racism and endorsing a non-discriminatory immigration policy was only the start of the debate. Hanson vowed to continue her campaign against the government's immigration and multicultural policies, despite warnings that her comments could be threatening Australia's relationship with Asia. Page 1.

Police have already identified a chief suspect responsible for a letter bomb which travelled from Malaysia to New Zealand, via Australia on two Qantas flights. The A4 envelope-sized bomb filled with explosives and metal shards, which appeared to be desiged to kill, remained undetected in Sydney and then Auckland, where it failed to detonate properly when opened. Page 1.

Retired New South Wales Supreme Court judge Justice David Yeldham yesterday adamantly denied allegations of paedophilia laid against him by Labor backbencher Franca Arena in state Parliament. New South Wales Premier Bob Carr and State Opposition Leader Peter Collins condemned the comments made by Arena during a speech about the conduct of the Police Royal Commission. Page 1.

Several hundred people waited outside the Sydney Entertainment Centre last night to catch a glimpse of Princess Diana, who was attending the Victor Chang Charity Ball. Diana was greeted by former New South Wales Premier and Victor Chang Cardiac Research Institute chairman Neville Wran, his wife Jill and 520 guests. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Tourism Council of Australia managing director Bruce Baird has linked cancellations of five Asian tour groups headed for Australia, including a party of 160 Singaporeans, to the worsening race debate sparked by Independent MP Pauline Hanson. In further warnings against intolerant views on race and immigration, Victoria Premier Jeff Kennett has suggested the Asian backlash could lead to a boycott of the Sydney Olympics and former Prime Minister Paul Keating has told a Jakarta business meeting Hanson's views are rooted in ignorance. Page 1.

As guest of honour at the Victor Chang Cardiac Research Institute charity night, the Princess of Wales drew a strong crowd, some big names and 810 diners to the A$1,000-a-plate gala dinner. The night will be aired on television tonight by the Nine Network whose owner, Kerry Packer, donated A$3 million to the institute after Chang performed life-saving bypass surgery on him in 1990. Page 1.

In the third railway explosion in just over a week, commuters were forced to flee St James Railway Station in Sydney after a bomb exploded in a toilet block. The explosion follows incidents at Central Station on Saturday and Circular Quay on Wednesday last week. All three have left police and authorities baffled by a motive for the attacks. Page 1.

New South Wales Upper House Labor backbencher Franca Arena named former Supreme Court judge David Yeldham QC and Independent MP for Wollongong Frank Arkell in questions relating to the New South Wales Police Royal Commission's paedophile hearings in Parliament yesterday. Page 1.
THE AGE

Foreshadowing a bipartisan resolution by State MPs condemning racial intolerance, to be voted on in the Victorian Parliament later this month, Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett yesterday said Independent MP Pauline Hanson's comments on immigration and race were out of touch with her own community and extremely dangerous. Page A1.

Victorian Transport Minister Alan Brown admitted yesterday that the state's Onelink public transport automatic ticketing system, originally scheduled for February 1995, would not be fully operational until the end of 1997. However Brown dismissed claims the delay would cost the government money, saying the government was not required to pay anything until the pilot scheme had been successfully installed. Page A1.

Under record quotas released last night by Primary Industries Minister John Anderson, Australia will export 6.25 million tonnes of hardwood chips each year. The decision was welcomed by the logging industry but Greens Senator Bob Brown said the new quotas guaranteed the devastation of Australian forests. Page A1.

Health authorities have banned the town of Dartmoor in western Victoria from using water for anything but firefighting or flushing toilets after an arsenic leak was detected at CSR's timber-processing plant last weekend near the bore that supplies the town's water. Page A1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
